links.outcome: Model performance disparities across sex, education, and socioeconomic subgroups
links.effect: All models showed minimal performance disparities across demographic and socioeconomic subgroups.
links.quote: All models demonstrated minimal performance disparities across demographic and socioeconomic subgroups, and SHAP analyses identified SBP, age, and BMI as consistently strong predictors.

links.outcome: Generalizability of discrimination in external validation on NHANES versus internal cohort
links.effect: ML models outperformed FRS (mean ROC AUC improvement up to 0.04, 95% CI not crossing zero), with robust generalizability confirmed in external validation.
links.quote: ML models, especially our ensembles and LightGBM, significantly outperformed FRS in discrimination (mean ROC AUC improvement up to 0.04, 95% CI not crossing zero), with robust generalizability confirmed in external validation.

screen.reason: The study develops and retrospectively evaluates ML models for hypertension risk, benchmarking against the Framingham Risk Score and performing fairness/subgroup analyses and external validation, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
